headline: Learned models couple generation and verification for small molecules and peptides
label: Learned Models For Molecular Prediction
summary: Learned predictors now drive ultra-large screening, generative design, and out-of-distribution generalization across small molecules and peptides.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learned representations, including ESM-2, ProtT5, and diffusion or latent-flow generators, applied to both prediction and design. Several items couple generation to verification: GenLoop iterates dtSFM outputs through AlphaFold 3 and developability filters, and ARCADIAMP pairs a discrete diffusion generator with an ESM2-based activity classifier for antimicrobial peptide design. AMPHORA conditions latent-flow generation on pathogen genome features and strain text. FastBindRank distills Boltz-2 binding predictions into a sequence-based surrogate trained on about 1% of PubChem for ultra-large screening. Others target generalization: active learning yields a 5-fold hit-rate gain in Borrelia HTS and 53-fold OOD enrichment. Not all items share this thread. The FEP+ macrocycle study is a retrospective free-energy benchmark with global pairwise RMSE of 1.06 kcal/mol, and several models, including the SVM QSAR classifiers and PredHLM, rely on descriptor-based inputs.
